name: DaggerDB
tagline: Real-time dimensional aggregator for .NET: an ACID columnar OLAP cube engine that never left preview.
description: DaggerDB is a small Swedish-made analytics engine for .NET that combines a column store with continuously maintained OLAP aggregates, so inserts arriving from a message queue are immediately reflected in dimensional queries without a separate cube-processing step. You define databases, dimensions, facts and measures in C#, commit data in transactions, and query through a fluent .NET API (select members, cross dimensions, filter), either in-process or against a DaggerDB server with a web admin console; cubes can be purely in memory or persistent. Version 1.0.1.0 (April 2015) added compressed bitmap indexes, a binary commit format and calculated measures, but it was explicitly labelled a preview not for production or commercial use, and no later release has appeared.
statusNote: Only a preview build (1.0.1.0, April 2015) was ever published, marked not for production; no updates since.

pricing.notes: Free preview download; commercial and production use not permitted.

strengths: Aggregates kept up to date on insert, so dashboards see new data immediately
Simple fluent C# API instead of MDX or cube-processing pipelines
Runs in-process or as a server, in memory or persisted
weaknesses: Never reached a stable release; preview license forbids production use
useCases: Historical reference for real-time aggregate cubes in .NET
